title: Recover dpkg and harden the remaining test timeouts
description: Follow-up from TASK-1.23 scope concerns: killing apt mid-install can leave dpkg interrupted for the next attempt, and runInSandbox still has the spawnSync-timeout weakness fixed for the speed-limits test.

nodes.title: Recover dpkg and harden the remaining test timeouts
Bootstrap the strict TypeScript project with one-command checks
Run every check in GitHub Actions on each push and pull request
Retry the stalled Playwright system-dependency install in CI
Keep strict wall-clock speed checks out of the CI test run

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given retry killed an apt attempt in the Playwright system-dependencies step, When the next attempt starts, Then sudo dpkg --configure -a runs first and an interrupted dpkg no longer fails the install
Given tests/support/sandbox.ts runInSandbox times out, When it stops the command, Then the whole process group is killed (via runProcessGroup), with a test using a grandchild that ignores SIGTERM

Given main CI run #73 needed 3 attempts (240 s, 240 s, then 164.5 s) for Playwright system dependencies, When the install step's attempt timeout and step timeout are re-tuned (or the apt packages are cached between runs), Then a typical install finishes within its first attempt and the step's total stays under its timeout-minutes

implementationNotes: AC#3 added 2026-11-19 from CI run #73 (main 769293f): TASK-1.23's sudo kill worked live twice, but attempts 1-2 hit the 240 s limit.
